name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q01 - Matching specific proteins to cellular functions

questiontext.text:
Match the proteins in List-I with their respective functions in List-II:

List-I (Protein) List-II (Function)
A. Collagen I. Enables glucose transport into cells
B. Trypsin II. Intercellular ground substance
C. Insulin III. Enzyme
D. GLUT-4 IV. Hormone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Physiological role of collagen
Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world and functions primarily as the structural intercellular ground substance in connective tissues.

Step 2: Biochemical nature of trypsin
Trypsin is a proteolytic digestive catalyst and is classified functionally as an enzyme.

Step 3: Endocrine function of insulin
Insulin is a peptide regulatory molecule secreted by the pancreas that acts as a hormone to regulate blood glucose homeostasis.

Step 4: Transporter function of GLUT-4
Glucose transporter type 4 (GLUT-4) is a specialized membrane transport protein that enables glucose transport into cells across the plasma membrane.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Collagen pairs with intercellular ground substance; Trypsin pairs with enzyme; Insulin pairs with hormone; GLUT-4 pairs with enabling glucose transport into cells.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q02 - Matching categories of secondary plant metabolites

questiontext.text:
Match the secondary metabolites in List-I with their appropriate categories in List-II:

List-I (Secondary Metabolite) List-II (Category)
A. Morphine I. Lectin
B. Concanavalin A II. Toxin
C. Ricin III. Drug
D. Vinblastin IV. Alkaloid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical classification of morphine
Morphine and codeine are nitrogenous, basic plant products categorized as alkaloids.

Step 2: Biochemical classification of Concanavalin A
Concanavalin A is a carbohydrate-binding plant protein classified as a lectin.

Step 3: Biological nature of ricin
Abrin and ricin are highly potent phytotoxins categorized biologically as toxins.

Step 4: Pharmacological grouping of vinblastin
Vinblastin (obtained from Catharanthus roseus) and curcumin are therapeutic agents grouped as drugs.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Morphine pairs with alkaloid; Concanavalin A pairs with lectin; Ricin pairs with toxin; Vinblastin pairs with drug.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q03 - Matching amino acid structures and characteristics

questiontext.text:
Match the amino acids in List-I with their characteristic side chain (R group) or chemical property in List-II:

List-I (Amino Acid) List-II (R Group / Chemical Property)
A. Glycine I. Hydrogen atom (\(-\text{H}\))
B. Alanine II. Methyl group (\(-\text{CH}_3\))
C. Serine III. Hydroxy methyl group (\(-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\))
D. Glutamic acid IV. Acidic amino acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural nature of glycine
Glycine is the simplest amino acid wherein the variable R group substituent on the \(\alpha\)-carbon is a single hydrogen atom (\(-\text{H}\)).

Step 2: Structural nature of alanine
Alanine is an aliphatic amino acid possessing a methyl group (\(-\text{CH}_3\)) as its variable R group.

Step 3: Structural nature of serine
Serine contains a hydroxy methyl side chain (\(-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\)), making it a polar hydroxyl-containing amino acid.

Step 4: Ionization property of glutamic acid
Glutamic acid carries two carboxyl groups and one amino group in its total molecular structure, which imparts an acidic character.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Glycine pairs with hydrogen atom; Alanine pairs with methyl group; Serine pairs with hydroxy methyl group; Glutamic acid pairs with acidic amino acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q04 - Matching enzyme classes to catalyzed reactions

questiontext.text:
Match the classes of enzymes in List-I with the types of reactions they catalyze in List-II:

List-I (Enzyme Class) List-II (Type of Reaction Catalyzed)
A. Transferases I. Catalyze linking together of two compounds (e.g., C-O, C-S, C-N, P-O bonds)
B. Hydrolases II. Removal of groups from substrates leaving double bonds by mechanisms other than hydrolysis
C. Lyases III. Hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, or C-C bonds
D. Ligases IV. Transfer of a chemical group (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrates

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reaction mechanism of transferases
Transferases catalyze the transfer of a functional group (G), other than hydrogen, from one substrate molecule to another (\(\text{S}-\text{G} + \text{S}' \rightarrow \text{S} + \text{S}'-\text{G}\)).

Step 2: Reaction mechanism of hydrolases
Hydrolases facilitate the cleavage of chemical bonds such as ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C-C, C-halide, or P-N bonds via the addition of water (hydrolysis).

Step 3: Reaction mechanism of lyases
Lyases catalyze the cleavage and elimination of specific groups from substrates through non-hydrolytic pathways, resulting in the generation of double bonds.

Step 4: Reaction mechanism of ligases
Ligases synthesize new bonds by coupling two molecular species together, typically forming C-O, C-S, C-N, or P-O linkages at the expense of high-energy phosphate bonds.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Transferases pair with group transfer; Hydrolases pair with hydrolytic cleavage of bonds; Lyases pair with non-hydrolytic removal of groups leaving double bonds; Ligases pair with joining of two compounds.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q05 - Matching levels of protein structural organization

questiontext.text:
Match the structural levels of protein organization in List-I with their characteristic features in List-II:

List-I (Structural Level) List-II (Characteristic Feature)
A. Primary structure I. Polypeptide folded upon itself like a hollow woolen ball; gives 3D view and biological activity
B. Secondary structure II. Spatial arrangement of multiple individual folded polypeptide subunits with respect to each other
C. Tertiary structure III. Positional information and specific linear sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide chain
D. Quaternary structure IV. Local folding of the polypeptide chain into right-handed helices or pleated sheets

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Architectural definition of primary structure
Primary structure represents the linear sequence of amino acids in a protein chain, providing positional information (which amino acid is first, second, etc.) from the N-terminal to the C-terminal end.

Step 2: Architectural definition of secondary structure
Secondary structure arises from regular hydrogen-bonded local folding patterns of the polypeptide backbone, predominantly forming right-handed helices and pleated sheets.

Step 3: Architectural definition of tertiary structure
Tertiary structure refers to the overall compact 3-dimensional conformation formed when the polypeptide folds back upon itself like a hollow woolen ball, creating active catalytic crevices required for biological activity.

Step 4: Architectural definition of quaternary structure
Quaternary structure represents the higher-order geometric assembly and spatial arrangement of two or more distinct folded polypeptide subunits, as exemplified by adult human haemoglobin.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Primary structure pairs with sequence and positional information; Secondary structure pairs with local folding into right-handed helices or pleated sheets; Tertiary structure pairs with hollow woolen ball 3D folding necessary for biological activity; Quaternary structure pairs with spatial arrangement of multiple subunits.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q06 - Matching cellular components to percentage abundance

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical components of a cell in List-I with their corresponding percent ranges of total cellular mass in List-II:

List-I (Component) List-II (% of Total Cellular Mass)
A. Water I. 70–90
B. Proteins II. 10–15
C. Nucleic acids III. 5–7
D. Carbohydrates IV. 3

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Cellular abundance of water
Water is the most abundant chemical in living organisms, accounting for 70 to 90 percent of the total cellular mass.

Step 2: Cellular abundance of proteins
Proteins constitute the second most abundant group of biomolecules in a cell, making up approximately 10 to 15 percent of total mass.

Step 3: Cellular abundance of nucleic acids
Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) comprise approximately 5 to 7 percent of the total cellular weight.

Step 4: Cellular abundance of carbohydrates
Carbohydrates represent approximately 3 percent of the total cellular mass (with lipids representing 2 percent and inorganic ions representing 1 percent).

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Water corresponds to 70–90 percent; Proteins correspond to 10–15 percent; Nucleic acids correspond to 5–7 percent; Carbohydrates correspond to 3 percent.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q07 - Matching biomolecules to their monomeric units

questiontext.text:
Match the polysaccharides in List-I with their characteristic structural units and properties in List-II:

List-I (Polysaccharide) List-II (Structural Unit / Property)
A. Inulin I. Complex homopolymer of amino-sugars found in arthropod exoskeleton
B. Cellulose II. Polymer of fructose
C. Chitin III. Plant storage polysaccharide that forms helices holding \(\text{I}_2\)
D. Starch IV. Linear glucose homopolymer that cannot hold \(\text{I}_2\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Composition of inulin
Inulin is a natural storage fructan and is defined as a homopolymer of fructose monosaccharide units.

Step 2: Structural property of cellulose
Cellulose is an unbranched homopolymer of glucose found in plant cell walls that lacks complex helical turns and therefore cannot trap iodine molecules (\(\text{I}_2\)).

Step 3: Composition of chitin
Chitin is a complex structural polysaccharide that forms the exoskeleton of arthropods and is predominantly a homopolymer composed of N-acetylglucosamine (an amino-sugar derivative).

Step 4: Structural property of starch
Starch is the primary energy reserve polysaccharide in plant tissues that forms secondary helical structures capable of holding iodine (\(\text{I}_2\)) molecules in its helical interior to give a blue color.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Inulin pairs with polymer of fructose; Cellulose pairs with linear glucose homopolymer unable to hold iodine; Chitin pairs with complex homopolymer of amino-sugars in arthropod exoskeletons; Starch pairs with plant storage polysaccharide forming helices holding iodine.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q08 - Matching enzymes to specific cofactor requirements

questiontext.text:
Match the cofactor terms and specific examples in List-I with their accurate biological descriptions in List-II:

List-I (Cofactor / Component) List-II (Description / Association)
A. Haem I. Metal ion forming coordination bonds with active site and substrate in carboxypeptidase
B. NAD / NADP II. Protein portion of an enzyme that becomes active only upon binding a cofactor
C. Zinc (\(\text{Zn}^{2+}\)) III. Tightly bound organic prosthetic group in peroxidase and catalase
D. Apoenzyme IV. Co-enzyme containing the vitamin niacin whose association with apoenzyme is transient

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical nature of haem as a cofactor
Haem is an iron-porphyrin organic compound that serves as a tightly integrated prosthetic group directly at the catalytic active site of catalase and peroxidase.

Step 2: Biochemical characteristics of NAD and NADP
Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and its phosphorylated form (NADP) are co-enzymes that bind transiently to apoenzymes during oxidation-reduction catalysis and contain the water-soluble vitamin niacin.

Step 3: Coordination chemistry of zinc
Zinc is an essential divalent inorganic metal ion cofactor that establishes coordination bonds with active site amino acid side chains and the substrate molecule within the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.

Step 4: Definition of the apoenzyme
The apoenzyme represents the purely proteinaceous, catalytically inactive portion of a conjugated enzyme which requires the association of an appropriate non-protein cofactor to become catalytically functional.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Haem pairs with tightly bound organic prosthetic group in peroxidase and catalase; NAD / NADP pairs with co-enzyme containing niacin with transient association; Zinc pairs with metal ion in carboxypeptidase; Apoenzyme pairs with protein portion of the enzyme.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q09 - Matching nitrogenous bases nucleosides and nucleotides

questiontext.text:
Match the nitrogenous compounds in List-I with their accurate chemical definitions in List-II:

List-I (Compound) List-II (Chemical Definition)
A. Adenine I. Heterocyclic pyrimidine nitrogen base found in RNA
B. Adenosine II. Nucleotide composed of adenine, ribose, and a phosphate group
C. Adenylic acid III. Heterocyclic substituted purine nitrogen base
D. Uracil IV. Nucleoside formed by attaching adenine to a ribose sugar

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural identity of adenine
Adenine is a bicyclic heterocyclic nitrogenous base belonging to the class of substituted purines.

Step 2: Structural identity of adenosine
When adenine is covalently attached via an N-glycosidic bond to a pentose sugar (ribose), the resulting molecule is a nucleoside named adenosine.

Step 3: Structural identity of adenylic acid
When a phosphate group is esterified to the sugar moiety of adenosine, the molecule becomes a complete nucleotide named adenylic acid (adenosine monophosphate).

Step 4: Structural identity of uracil
Uracil is a monocyclic heterocyclic nitrogenous base belonging to the substituted pyrimidines, found specifically in ribonucleic acid (RNA) instead of thymine.

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Adenine pairs with heterocyclic substituted purine nitrogen base; Adenosine pairs with nucleoside formed by attaching adenine to ribose; Adenylic acid pairs with nucleotide composed of adenine, ribose, and a phosphate group; Uracil pairs with heterocyclic pyrimidine nitrogen base found in RNA.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOMOLECULES_Q10 - Matching elements to abundance in crust

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical elements in List-I with their corresponding percent weights in the Earth's crust in List-II:

List-I (Element) List-II (% Weight of Earth's Crust)
A. Oxygen (O) I. 27.7
B. Silicon (Si) II. 46.6
C. Carbon (C) III. 0.14
D. Hydrogen (H) IV. 0.03

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Crustal abundance of oxygen
Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust, constituting 46.6 percent of its total weight (compared to 65.0 percent in the human body).

Step 2: Crustal abundance of silicon
Silicon is the second most abundant element in the Earth's crust, accounting for 27.7 percent of crustal weight, whereas its concentration in living human tissue is negligible.

Step 3: Crustal abundance of carbon
Carbon is a trace element in non-living crustal matter, contributing only 0.03 percent of the Earth's crust by weight (compared to 18.5 percent in the human body).

Step 4: Crustal abundance of hydrogen
Hydrogen contributes 0.14 percent of the weight of the Earth's crust (compared to 9.5 percent in the human body).

Step 5: Final conceptual pairing
Oxygen pairs with 46.6 percent; Silicon pairs with 27.7 percent; Carbon pairs with 0.03 percent; Hydrogen pairs with 0.14 percent.
